title: Feature Bento: modular quick-win feature bundles (brain dump)
body:
One-pager / messy brain dump for Feature Bento — small, packaged feature bundles that product teams can toggle on for customers (aim: reduce time-to-value, guardrails included).

Context / problem:
- We keep building single large features that take months; customers want tiny opinionated feature packs they can enable quickly.
- Common asks: better session defaults, canned fallback strategies, lightweight cost controls, out-of-the-box retry/backoff for streaming.
- Engineering overhead for each small feature is high due to rollout, docs, and console wiring.

Vision:
- Deliver 4–6 curated "bento" bundles (each ~1–2 week dev work) that combine runtime behavior + console defaults + API contract + docs + presets.
- Teams install/enroll customers to a bento; analytics + safe defaults + upgrade path to full product features.

Target users / personas:
- Platform/PMs at startups: want low-friction features to show value quickly.
- Devs integrating Redwood API: want plug-and-play behaviors without deep tuning.
- Enterprise SREs: want predictable, documented defaults and SLA-friendly fallbacks.

Candidate bentos (first pass):
1) Frugal-Fidelity Bento: auto-downshift to quantized small models for long conversations + prefix caching heuristics.
   - quick win: reduce per-token cost ~20% for chat workloads.
2) Conversational Guardrail Bento: structured tool-calling templates + safety filters + fallback to non-actionable response.
3) Latency-SLA Bento: per-route fast-path routing + small-batch synchronous mode + metrics shipping + circuit-breaker.
4) Session Saver Bento: snapshot-on-inactivity + compact recaps + sticky persona anchoring.
5) Developer Debug Bento: verbose telemetry, request replay links, sample prompt snapshots (dev-only).

For each bento include:
- Runtime toggles (detailed list to hand to infra): kernel preference, batching targets, kv-cache TTL, fallback variant map
- Console defaults & UX: toggle, short description, risk level, estimated cost delta, example request/response
- API flag: bento="frugal-fidelity-v1" or X-Redwood-Bento header.
- Docs snippet + quickstart code (one-liner to enable).
- Safety/limits: max tokens, rate uplift, when to disable.
- Migration path: how to extract and own the feature if customer wants to customize.

Example user story (Frugal-Fidelity):
- As a PM at a marketplace startup, I want chat sessions to cost less on average while keeping user-facing quality, so I can scale usage for free-tier users.
- Acceptance criteria:
  - mean tokens/response cost reduced by >=15% on targeted cohort in 2-week A/B test
  - less than 1.5x increase in user-visible latency (p50/p95 measured)
  - < 2% negative quality regression by automated eval set

Console UX sketch (notes):
- Add a "Feature Bento" section under Routes > Presets. Each bento card shows: short description, cost delta, risk slider (low/med/high), toggle + rollout (%).
- Click card -> small modal with API flag and example curl + link to telemetry filters.

API sample (rusty pseudocode in docs):
- Header: "X-Redwood-Bento: frugal-fidelity-v1"
- OR body param: { "bento": "latency-sla-v1", "route": "chat-1" }

Metrics to gather per-bento:
- adoption_rate (routes/users with bento enabled)
- cost_delta_per_token vs baseline (approx $/1k tokens)
- quality_metrics: automatic eval loss + spot human evals
- latency p50/p95/p99 and cold-start spike count
- fallback_count (times route swapped to lower variant)

Rollout strategy (rough):
- Phase 0: internal alpha (SE + a few power users).
- Phase 1: opt-in in Console (beta) for new orgs + 1% of existing orgs via canary routing.
- Phase 2: gradual ramp with safety guardrails + automated rollback if quality regressions triggered.

Experiment matrix (A/B ideas):
- A: control baseline; B: frugal-fidelity bento for long sessions only (session len>150 tokens). Measure cost and quality.
- A/B2: latency-sla bento vs prioritized route w/o batching; measure p95 improvements and cost tradeoffs.

Dependencies / infra needs:
- Runtime: simple feature flag routing and per-request bento header parse. Minimal kernel changes for variant selection.
- Console: new UI cards + telemetry grouping and aggregated cost deltas per-bento.
- Billing/quotas: show projected cost estimates per-org when enabling bentos.

Open questions / risks (frank):
- Quality regressions are hard to catch automatically; need evaluation harness + targeted human spot checks.
- Support burden if many bentos ramp and customers ask for custom variants. Need migration docs.
- Billing ambiguity: show "estimated" savings, not guaranteed. Legal care.

Next actions / TODOs:
- [ ] Draft PRD skeleton for top-2 bentos (Frugal-Fidelity, Latency-SLA). (owner: Asha)
- [ ] Quick telemetry prototype to compute cost_delta for a sample org (owner: Omar)
- [ ] Console card mockups (owner: Nora)
- [ ] Create JIRA epic and link (INFER-1892 placeholder)
- [ ] Small internal alpha invite list + script for feedback collection

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Could use model-variant marketplace internally: bentos are just recipes combining runtime variant + console preset + doc + eval set.
- For developer debug bento, ensure we have opt-out for customers who disallow expanded telemetry.
- Consider adding "bento studio" later to let customers author their own bundles (longer term).

Fragments I want to paste elsewhere:
- "bento" = opinionated, low-config packaged feature for quick enablement
- acceptance signal: clear metric and rollback path

Links / references:
- initial convo in Slack: #prod-feature-bento (thread pinned)
- related doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/FRUGAL-42 (metrics calc)
- similar ideation scratch: /shared_drives/product/quickwins/mini-bundles-notes (need to pull)

Unresolved micro-decisions:
- header vs body param for API; header seems cleaner for proxies/sidecars
- default rollout percentage for new bentos: 10%? or 25% to get signals faster

Rough schedule idea (6 weeks for a first bento):
- wk1: design + telemetry prototype + PRD
- wk2: runtime + API parse + basic variant wiring
- wk3: eval harness + console card mockup
- wk4: alpha internal + bugfix
- wk5: limited external beta (10% of opt-in orgs)
- wk6: measure, iterate, decide GA

Random brain-snippets:
- Keep the bento surface intentionally small: 3 toggles max for initial one.
- Surface example customer case studies in console card to aid adoption.
- We should add a built-in "safety net" that runs a lightweight quality test on enable and warns if regression is seen within first 24h.

-- end --
